BE Group AB Announces Major Expansion to Meet Rising Steel Demand in Sweden

Swedish steel processing specialist BE Group AB has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its production capacity in response to robust demand from the construction and manufacturing sectors. The investment, valued at approximately SEK 120 million, will see the company upgrade its Malmö facility and add new processing equipment over the next 18 months.

“Demand for high-quality steel products continues to grow, particularly from regional manufacturers and infrastructure projects,” said Johan Lindqvist, BE Group AB’s Chief Executive Officer, at a press conference on Thursday. “This investment will enable us to better serve our customers and strengthen our position as a leading supplier in southern Sweden.”

The expansion includes the installation of advanced cutting and surface treatment lines, as well as upgrades to the company’s logistics center to streamline deliveries. BE Group AB estimates the project will create up to 25 new jobs, primarily in operations and logistics.

Local officials welcomed the announcement. “This is excellent news for Malmö and Skåne County,” said Annika Sandström, Chair of the Malmö Business Development Council. “The new jobs and increased industrial activity will benefit the region at a time when sustainable growth is a top priority.”

Industry observers note that Sweden’s steel sector has seen steady growth over the past five years, driven by investments in renewable energy, transport, and housing. “Companies like BE Group AB are responding to a clear need for reliable supply chains and high-quality steel products,” said Lars Ekström, an analyst at the Swedish Metals Trade Association.

BE Group AB expects the first phase of the expansion to be operational by spring next year. The company, which employs around 700 people nationwide, has emphasized its commitment to sustainability and energy efficiency in the new development.

“We are focused on minimizing our environmental impact while supporting Sweden’s industrial future,” Lindqvist added.
